newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.KOREAN WON ENDS LOWER ON DOLLAR BUILD-UPS.
newsitem.headline: S.KOREAN WON ENDS LOWER ON DOLLAR BUILD-UPS.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar on Tuesday due to importer settlements and build-ups of dollar positions, dealers said.
"Dollar positions are rapidly drying up because of continuing importer deals," said a foreign bank dealer.
The won closed at 894.60 against Monday's closing of 893.50. It opened at 894.00 and moved between 893.80 and 894.70.
Dealers said dollar buying was limited by fears of the central bank's dollar sales intervention.
"The intervention level is believed to be at around the 895.00 level," the foreign bank dealer said.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 894.40 on Wednesday, compared with 893.00 today.
Dealers said the yen's fall against the dollar also helped the won open weak today.
"Market players will continue to watch the yen's movements against the dollar," said a domestic bank dealer said.
He said trading would range from 893.50 to 896.50 on Wednesday.
